name: TLC555CDR
title: TLC555 CMOS timer
summary: A CMOS version of the 555 timer, pin for pin and function for function interchangeable with the NE555. It runs from a single 2 V to 15 V supply, draws about 1 mW at 5 V, has picoamp trigger and threshold inputs that suit small timing capacitors, and oscillates at up to 2.1 MHz typical. The output swings to both rails, sinking 100 mA and sourcing 10 mA typical. Grades C, I, M and Q cover 0 °C to 70 °C, -40 °C to 85 °C, -55 °C to 125 °C and -40 °C to 125 °C; TLC555CDR is the C grade in SOIC-8 on tape and reel.
key_figures: 2 V to 15 V (C); 3 V (I) or 5 V (M, Q) minimum
180 µA typ, 350 µA max at 5 V, 25 °C
20 ns / 15 ns typ (RL = 10 MΩ, CL = 10 pF)
SOIC-8, PDIP-8, SO-8, TSSOP-14, CDIP-8, LCCC-20

notes: The suffix letter after TLC555 is the temperature grade: C 0 °C to 70 °C, I -40 °C to 85 °C, M -55 °C to 125 °C (military, QML), Q -40 °C to 125 °C (automotive). The letters after it name the package: D SOIC-8, P PDIP-8, PS SO-8, PW TSSOP-14, JG CDIP-8, FK LCCC-20; a trailing R is tape and reel.
5962-89503012A is marked as the TLC555MFKB, and 5962-8950301PA as the TLC555MJGB.
Two markings in one cell are two lines of one marking.
Other qualified versions: TLC555-Q1 (automotive, AEC-Q100) and TLC555M (military, QML).

circuits.title: Monostable operation
circuits.description: One-shot. At rest OUT is low and DISCH holds the timing capacitor C empty. A low-going pulse on TRIG sets the latch: OUT rises, DISCH lets go, and C charges through RA until THRES reaches the CONT level, at which point OUT falls and C is dumped. The pulse lasts about 1.1 RA C whatever the supply, provided the supply holds steady through the interval. RESET is tied to VDD and CONT has a capacitor to ground.
notes: Output pulse duration tw ≈ 1.1 × RA × C.
Typical waveforms at RA = 9.1 kΩ, CL = 0.01 µF: input and output 2 V/div, 0.1 ms/div.

circuits.title: Astable operation
circuits.description: Free-running oscillator. TRIG and THRES are joined on the timing capacitor C, which charges through RA plus RB and discharges through RB alone into DISCH, so it swings between about 1/3 and 2/3 of VDD. OUT is high while C charges and low while it discharges; RA and RB together set the duty cycle, and the frequency does not depend on the supply. VDD has a 0.01 µF bypass; CONT is left open in this connection, and a capacitor from CONT to ground improves operation.
notes: Typical waveforms at RA = 5 kΩ, RB = 3 kΩ, C = 0.15 µF: 1 V/div, 0.5 ms/div.

circuits.title: Frequency divider (divide by three)
circuits.description: The monostable connection driven by a pulse train, with RA and C set so that the output runs at one third of the input frequency. A trigger arriving while a cycle is timing does not restart it.
notes: Waveforms at 2 V/div, 0.1 ms/div.

circuits.title: Missing-pulse detector
circuits.description: A monostable that is restarted by every input pulse. The input drives TRIG and also the base of a PNP transistor across the timing capacitor, so each low-going input pulse empties C and starts the interval again. While pulses keep arriving closer together than the interval, OUT stays high; a late pulse, a missing one or a stopped train lets C reach the threshold and OUT goes low. A fault shows only if it leaves the input high; a low-stuck input keeps C empty and goes undetected.
notes: Choose RA × C longer than the longest normal input high time.
Timing waveforms at VDD = 5 V, RA = 1 kΩ, C = 0.1 µF: 2 V/div, 0.1 ms/div.

circuits.title: Pulse-width modulation
circuits.description: A monostable clocked on TRIG by a steady pulse train, with a modulating voltage on CONT moving the threshold. Each clock edge starts a pulse whose length follows the CONT voltage, so the output duty cycle tracks the modulation, though not linearly, because C charges along an exponential.
notes: The modulation may reach CONT directly or through a capacitor; when direct, its voltage and source impedance shift the timer's bias.
Choose RA × C equal to or shorter than the clock period.
The clock's low level must sit under 1/3 VDD and its high level above it, and its low time must be shorter than the shortest output high time, which favours a clock that is high most of the time.
The lowest modulation voltage recommended is 1 V; below it the threshold comparator's delay and storage time grow sharply.
Duty cycles under 10% give irregular pulses; approaching 100% the output divides the clock by 2, then 3, then 4.

circuits.title: Pulse-position modulation
circuits.description: The astable connection with a modulating voltage on CONT. Moving CONT shifts both capacitor thresholds, so each cycle's delay, and with it frequency and duty, follow the modulation.
notes: The modulation may reach CONT directly or through a capacitor; when direct, its voltage and source impedance shift the timer's bias.
With CONT at 2/3 VDD the frequency and duty cycle follow the astable equations.
A control voltage under 1 V can produce glitches in place of a clean pulse stream.

circuits.title: Sequential timer
circuits.description: Three monostables in a chain. Closing S briefly pulls the first TRIG low and starts output A. When output A falls, the 0.001 µF capacitor and 33 kΩ resistor into the next stage turn that edge into a short low pulse of about 10 µs on its TRIG, which starts output B; B ending starts C the same way. Each 1N4148 keeps its TRIG from being driven above VDD when the previous output rises. Each stage's interval is 1.1 R C.
notes: twA = 1.1 RA CA, twB = 1.1 RB CB, twC = 1.1 RC CC.
Waveforms at 5 V/div, 1 s/div.

circuits.title: ESD test schematic
circuits.description: Test board for the three pins most often exposed, RESET, TRIG and OUT. Each line has a 1000 pF capacitor to ground at its test point, series resistance, and a pair of BAT54W Schottky diodes clamping it to VDD and to ground; RESET and TRIG also have a 100 kΩ pull-up and 10.0 kΩ to ground, and TRIG is fed through a 0.1 µF series capacitor. The supply enters on J1 and J2 with 10 µF and 0.1 µF bypass and an SMBJ15A transient suppressor; each clamp pair has its own 1000 pF from VDD to ground. CONT has 0.01 µF to ground, and the timing node is 10.0 kΩ from VDD with 1000 pF to ground.
notes: Levels reached with this board are in the ESD test results table: 12 kV with every part fitted at 5 V or 15 V, 8 kV at 5 V with the diodes D1 to D7 left off.
Protection by passive parts alone is not recommended on a single 15 V supply, since the higher voltage lets too much current flow through the device.

equations.note: An output duty cycle below 50% needs tc(H) / tc(L) < 1 and may need RA ≤ ron.

where.R: stage timing resistor (RA, RB or RC)
where.C: stage timing capacitor (CA, CB or CC)

operation.text: A CMOS version of the 555 timer with the NE555 pinout and function, usable for timing up to about 2.1 MHz. Every input responds to level, not to edges. The very high input impedance of TRIG and THRES allows smaller timing capacitors than a bipolar NE555 or LM555 and so more accurate delays and oscillations. Supply current is low over the whole supply range.

An internal divider of three matched resistors puts the trigger level near 1/3 VDD and the threshold level near 2/3 VDD; a voltage on CONT moves both. The resistor values change with VDD and temperature but track one another closely, so the ratio stays stable. TRIG falling below the trigger level sets the latch and drives OUT high. With TRIG above its level and THRES above the threshold, the latch resets and OUT goes low. Whenever OUT is low, DISCH is a low-impedance path to GND.
RESET overrides TRIG, and TRIG overrides THRES when CONT is at 2/3 VDD. Inputs that are not used must be tied to a suitable logic level, or false triggering can result.

A cycle starts when TRIG drops below the trigger level and ends only if TRIG has returned high no later than 1 µs ahead of the interval's end. With TRIG held at ground the comparator storage time can reach 1 µs, which sets the shortest monostable pulse at 1 µs. Threshold and charging current both scale with VDD, so the interval does not depend on the supply provided it stays constant during the cycle.

A low-going pulse applied to RESET and TRIG together during an interval empties C and starts a fresh cycle on the rising edge of the reset pulse; OUT stays low while RESET is low. When RESET is driven by logic or a microcontroller, a pull-up to VDD (10 kΩ, for example) keeps it from floating; when the function is not wanted, RESET is wired straight to VDD. Holding the part in reset forces OUT and DISCH low and lowers supply current slightly.

operation.topic: Setting the trigger level in a monostable
operation.text: The trigger trip point can be set by a voltage on CONT. A voltage of 10% to 80% of the supply from a resistor divider carrying at least 500 µA gives good results.

The simple astable equations leave out the TRIG/THRES-to-DISCH propagation delays, which lengthen the period and let the capacitor charge past its level, so the error grows with frequency; the discharge switch resistance ron also adds to RB and matters when RB is small. The high-frequency forms of tc(H) and tc(L) include both. CT should count board stray capacitance as well as the fitted capacitor. A decoupling capacitor on CONT also shifts the duty cycle by an amount that depends on its leakage resistance. Near 50% duty a fixed constant may stand in for the log terms.

The minimum supply is 2 V, 3 V or 5 V according to the coldest ambient the grade supports, and the maximum is 15 V. Bypass the supply with at least a 0.1 µF ceramic in parallel with a 1 µF electrolytic, placed as close to the part as possible on short traces; good bypassing protects the surrounding circuit and keeps the output pulses stable.

The 0.1 µF ceramic and 1 µF electrolytic bypass capacitors sit right at the VDD pin, and the timing capacitor goes close to DISCH. A bottom-layer ground plane improves noise immunity and signal integrity. The basic layout uses C1 for the timing capacitor, C2 0.01 µF from CONT to ground, C3 0.1 µF ceramic and C4 1 µF electrolytic for supply bypass, and R1 as the timing resistor.

The built-in HBM and CDM protection is enough for assembly under ESD control. Where RESET, TRIG or OUT are exposed to discharges in use, extra protection is strongly recommended: bypass capacitors, series resistors and clamping diodes, as on the ESD test board.
